question: Valence electrons are present in the:

options.text: innermost as well as outermost shell of an atom

solution:
The correct answer is the __**Outermost shell of an atom**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• ** ****Valence electrons **are the electrons located at the **outermost shell of an atom****.**
 
• These **electrons play a crucial role** in chemical reactions and determine how an atom forms bonds with other atoms
 
• The e**lectrons present in the inner shell** are core electrons.
 
• Valence electrons are all arranged in different orbitals or shells and are mostly **negatively charged particles.**
 
• One of the easiest ways to find valence electrons is by checking out the **elements’ place in the periodic table. **
 
• The valency of an element is
 
 
• Equal to the number of valence electrons
 
• Equal to the number of electrons required to complete eight electrons in the valence shell.
 
 
 
• Valency of a metal=No. of Valence electrons
 
• Valency Of a non-metal=8-No. of valence electrons
 
• **For Ex**:
 
 
• **Sodium**(Z=11) Electronic Configuration=2,8,1
 
 
• Valency=1
 
 
 
• **Magnesium**(Z=2) Electronic Configuration=2,8,2
 
 
• Valency=2
 
 
 
• **Chlorine**(Z=17) Electronic Configuration=2,8,7
 
 
• Valency=8-7=1
 
 
 
• **Oxygen**=16 Electronic Configuration=2,8,6
 
 
• Valency=8-6=2
